The sick people are spread across 17 states

![Image 1: Patient count for parasite outbreak linked to lettuce tops 10,000](https://storage.ghost.io/c/43/4e/434e508a-5e2f-4102-a53d-00bca10bb4bf/content/images/size/w30/2026/08/Cyclospora-map-08-21-26.png)

Published:August 21, 2026, 8:38 pm

## Subscribe to Food Safety News

Get the free version of our newsletter. No spam ever, unsubscribe anytime.

The patient count for an outbreak of infections from the Cyclospora parasite linked to iceberg lettuce has topped 10,000.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is reporting 10,930 patients as of Aug. 21, up from 9,481 reported on Aug. 13. The sick people are spread across 17 states. There are 454 patients who have required hospitalization and two from Michigan have died. Illnesses linked to this outbreak began on June 14 and onset dates have continued through Aug.11.

The outbreak includes people who reported exposure to processed iceberg lettuce from the Taylor Farms growing and processing operation in Central Mexico and served or purchased at various locations, including people who previously reported eating at Taco Bell. Most of these illnesses began before the Taylor Farms iceberg lettuce recall on July 17.

The Food and Drug Administration has begun inspecting the implicated Taylor Farms lettuce growing and production operation.

A recent report by the Government Accountability Office found that FDA averaged only 917 foreign food-facility inspections annually from fiscal years 2018 through 2023 — less than 5 percent of the statutory target established under the Food Safety Modernization Act.

The Taylor Farms operation in question had not been inspected by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for seven years

Imagine being the parent of an infant and learning that the baby formula in your home may be associated with a life-threatening illness. You rush to the pantry and begin looking for which product codes are associated with a recall notice web site, and you can’t find the codes. Perhaps the container has already been discarded but you know you have used that brand. Perhaps you never even heard about the recall until after the product had been consumed and you’re at the hospital with your sick infant.

In June 2026, Nara Organics recalled all lots of its powdered infant formula after FDA investigated four confirmed cases of infant botulism among infants who had consumed the product. The recall was announced quickly, but issuing a recall and reaching every household that may still possess the product are not the same thing.

That distinction is not theoretical. During a the ByHeart infant formula recall, FDA found recalled product

[remaining on retail shelves after retailers had already been notified](https://www.fda.gov/food/outbreaks-foodborne-illness/outbreak-investigation-infant-botulism-infant-formula-november-2025?ref=foodsafetynews.com)
